findings.issue: 途端 is labeled an adverb, but it is a noun that only works bound to a preceding past-tense clause (〜た途端). The lesson body itself contrasts them ('突然 é um advérbio solto' / '途端 precisa de outra ação'), so the objective (and the matching checklist line) contradicts the prose.
findings.current: Distinguir os advérbios 突然, 途端 e とにかく
findings.suggested: Distinguir os advérbios 突然 e とにかく do substantivo 途端 (usado em 〜た途端)

findings.issue: In a sentence about giving up one's seat, bare 年寄り reads as blunt/impolite; the standard collocation taught to learners is お年寄りに席を譲る. Suggest adding the honorific お (reading would become おとしよりにせきをゆずってごらん).
findings.current: <jp reading="としよりにせきをゆずってごらん">年寄りに席を譲ってごらん</jp>
findings.suggested: <jp reading="おとしよりにせきをゆずってごらん">お年寄りに席を譲ってごらん</jp>

findings.issue: 途端 is a noun that only occurs bound to a preceding た-clause (〜た途端), not an adverb like 突然/とにかく. The lesson's own pitfall note says 途端 cannot stand alone, contradicting this label.
findings.current: Distinguir os advérbios 突然, 途端 e とにかく
findings.suggested: Distinguir os advérbios 突然 e とにかく do substantivo 途端, que só aparece em 〜た途端

findings.issue: In a 'give up your seat' context the standard, respectful Japanese is お年寄り; bare 年寄り sounds blunt/disrespectful when referring to the elderly person being helped, so the example models bad register.
findings.current: <jp reading="としよりにせきをゆずってごらん">年寄りに席を譲ってごらん</jp>
findings.suggested: <jp reading="おとしよりにせきをゆずってごらん">お年寄りに席を譲ってごらん</jp>

findings.issue: Authoring-side instruction leaks into learner prose: the learner is told to 'use the grammar to give tips in the examples', but the examples are already written for them. Confusing and ungrammatical as learner-facing text.
findings.current: Aproveite a gramática deste tópico de conselho e permissão, como ～てごらん (experimenta) e ～ことだ (o ideal é), para dar dicas nos exemplos.
findings.suggested: Os exemplos abaixo reaproveitam a gramática de conselho deste tópico, como ～てごらん (experimenta) e ～ことだ (o ideal é).
